taxonomyNote: Aquarium fighting conchs are Strombus alatus Gmelin, 1791 (Florida fighting conch) or Strombus pugilis Linnaeus, 1758 (West Indian fighting conch). WoRMS/MolluscaBase currently lists S. alatus as a junior synonym of S. pugilis; both stay in Strombus (Aliger holds the related queen conch group).

referenceSize.note: Shell length apex to siphonal canal tip. Malacolog / Wikipedia record S. alatus shells to 112 mm; 7 to 8 cm is a typical aquarium adult. The shell spans 8.0 cm along its own axis (7.5 cm projected on X at the 20 degree resting pitch); in the rest pose the eyes peer about 6 mm ahead of the canal tip, so the measured X extent is 8.1 cm, within the 3 percent gate of the shell length.

shell.notes: Dextral conispiral, 8 whorls, whorl expansion 1.85 per turn, spire angle about 57 degrees from dropRatio and centerOffsetRatio. Body whorl elongated anteriorly (lowerSemiAxisRatioBody) into a short siphonal canal; 9 blunt shoulder knobs per whorl on the last 2.8 whorls; flared thick outer lip with a posterior wing and the stromboid notch on the anterior part of the lip.

visualDebt: Shell is one self-overlapping closed loft: whorls overlap inside the shell as in life, but the union surface is not resolved, so the suture is a geometric step rather than a modelled channel.
Shoulder knobs are ring displacements at 64 rings per whorl, so they read as blunt scallops rather than sculpted nodules; the 36-segment rings show mild faceting on the ramp.
Operculum serrations and the mantle edge are not modelled; the sickle operculum is a smooth flattened tube.
Eye pattern is a texture on an ellipsoid (no separate cornea); eyestalks retract by bone scaling, which also shrinks the eye.

Eyestalk versus shell clearance is not declared: during withdraw the retracting stalks pass the parietal wall inside the aperture region. Eyestalks are proven clear of the foot, the proboscis and each other in every clip.
Shell colour is procedural mottling with flammules and spiral bands, not a calibrated pattern from a specific specimen.
